title: Core Validation 008 — Certified Adaptive Functional Atoms
decision_question: Under real frozen Pythia representations, can replay-free subspace certificates support a sparse compositional low-rank functional basis with better reuse/growth behavior than rank-1 fragmentation or a monolithic certified transform?

hypothesis.primary: Functional memory is better modeled as a sparse composition of certified low-rank atoms than as a hard semantic/functional partition.
hypothesis.rank_question: Rank-1 is treated as the smallest natural write primitive, not as an assumed persistent Cell boundary; fixed rank-1, rank-2, rank-4 and adaptive-rank atom caps are compared under the same conceptual factor-parameter budget.
hypothesis.growth_question: Growth is triggered when the desired local write cannot be represented or safely absorbed by existing atoms under their protected dependency subspaces.

representation.write_demand: G = mean_t[(U^T dL/dh_t) z_t^T] on the frozen foundation path
representation.target_normalization: G / max(||G||_F, eps) so primary geometry is not confounded by the weak whole-model Cell effect observed in the preflight bridge
representation.local_action: for sequence activation rows Z, compare Z G^T and Z G_hat^T

certificate.learner_state: per-atom bounded z covariance plus derived Q; no historical examples, labels, raw activations or replay buffer
certificate.safe_update: Delta B = rank_r_approx(R P_free), hence Delta B Q ~= 0
certificate.growth_signal: spawn when sparse reconstruction remains above threshold and no existing selected atom can safely reduce the residual enough
certificate.hidden_evaluator: may retain exact historical z rows only to measure false-safe drift; these rows cannot influence routing, updates, growth or thresholds

composition.oracle_training_assignment: OMP-style signed sparse coefficients over current atoms using write-demand geometry; target-dependent and non-deployable
composition.deployable_router: ridge map from pooled frozen z to final oracle coefficient vectors, followed by top-k sparsification

budget.accounting: each added rank unit costs 2*d factor scalars; with d=64 this allows at most 32 rank units, approximately one dense 64x64 Cell

primary_metrics: heldout oracle normalized Frobenius reconstruction residual
secondary_metrics: whole-model NLL is diagnostic only and is not a Core 008 support gate

confirmation_gates.comparative_rule_rank1: adaptive must have <= 0.85x rank1 deploy local-action residual OR <= 0.75x rank1 spawn rate, while the other quantity is <= 1.10x rank1
confirmation_gates.comparative_rule_monolithic: adaptive must have <= 0.80x monolithic unresolved-write fraction OR <= 0.85x monolithic deploy local-action residual, while certificate safety remains within the same absolute gate

interpretation_boundary: A positive result would support sparse compositional certified functional atoms in this frozen-representation linear-write setting; it would not establish end-to-end Transformer continual learning.
A rank-1 failure with adaptive-rank success would reject rank-1 as the persistent atom boundary without rejecting rank-1 as an elementary write primitive.
A monolithic failure with compositional success would support growth by local safe-write infeasibility rather than hard semantic/function labels.
A failure of all variants would be evidence against the current write-demand/certificate geometry and should block further architectural elaboration.
